messages:
mina: Noticing odd reordering when we onboard nebula-v2-int8 on the rtl+cjk mixed benchmark. Sentences near Arabic-CJK boundaries get swapped and sometimes a stray "[SPLIT]" token appears. BLEU drops ~4.2 pts on mix-bidi-dev. :frowning:

jorge: Can you paste a tiny repro and the delta?

mina: Repro (baseline fp16 -> nebula-v2-int8):
```
input: "السلام عليكم\n\u4e16\u754c\u3002\nمرحبا"
baseline: "Peace be upon you. 世界. Hello"
nebula-v2-int8: "Peace be upon you. [SPLIT] Hello 世界."
```
BLEU: baseline 29.4 -> int8 25.2 on mix-bidi-dev (n=1.5k). Exact match drop ~12%.

sophie: That [SPLIT] looks like our tokenization placeholder for unexpected bidirectional joins. Any tokenizer logs?

mina: Tokenizer showed inserted U+2066/U+2069 markers around the CJK sequence only on int8 build. Token ids: [512, 0x2066, 4092, 4093, 118].

jorge: Could be the quantized encoder chunking where caching expects LTR contexts. Did you try forcing the classical attention path (no fused-attn) to see if it's a runtime kernel swap?

mina: Quick A/B: forcing classical attention + reference merge removes the split token and ordering looks like baseline (BLEU 29.0). So runtime kernel selection + token merge seems implicated.

build-bot: Canary report: nebula-v2-int8 (canary-3) failed mix-bidi-detok smoke (delta BLEU -4.2). Auto-rollback triggered.

jorge: OK. Hypothesis: int8 quant kernels for chunked attention don't correctly propagate directional embedding boundaries, causing insertion of directionality control placeholders in the detok path. I'll reproduce locally with --trace-tokenizer and attach traces.

mina: Repro steps I used:
1) image: redwood/nebula-v2-int8:2026-03-21-canary
2) ./run_repro.sh --dataset mix-bidi-dev --num 100 --trace-tokenizer > repro.log
3) compare to redwood/nebula-v2-fp16:stable
Attached a sample from repro.log with raw bytes: e3 80 82 0a d8 a7 d9 84 (CJK period, newline, Arabic alif lam).

sophie: Could also be detok mapping treating U+2066/U+2069 as literal tokens after quant kernel reordering. Add a unit test for bidi boundary preservation in token-level merges. We'll also add a small eval that runs on every build (mix-bidi-detok) in ml-ci.

ml-ci: New job queued: mix-bidi-detok-smoke (runs on PRs that touch runtime kernels).

jorge: Plan: bisect the int8 attention packing changes, add assert to ensure that direction-control codepoints are not emitted by the tokenizer merge step, and add regression unit test. If we confirm kernel-level bug, we'll gate the fused-attn selection until fixed.

mina: Uploaded 50 failing excerpts to the issue with logs and repro commands. For now keeping canary rolled back.

sophie: Also note: this surfaced only on mixed RTL+CJK pairs; pure Arabic or pure CJK tests were fine. That suggests the boundary handling path is the culprit.

mina: TL;DR: nebula-v2-int8 introduces detok split/order glitches around Arabic<->CJK boundaries; workaround is to avoid fused int8 kernels / use reference merge + classical attention until kernel fix + unit tests landed.
